queries.title: Which heroes do developers touch the most?
queries.question: Per game, which heroes were changed most often, and are they mostly being buffed or nerfed?
queries.why: Frequent changes signal a hero the developers can't get right, a design problem rather than a numbers problem.
queries.sql:
SELECT
    game,
    hero,
    COUNT(*)                                          AS total_changes,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'buff')      AS buffs,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'nerf')      AS nerfs,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type IN ('rework', 'adjustment')) AS reworks_or_adjustments,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'buff')
      - COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE change_type = 'nerf')  AS net_direction,   -- >0 = mostly buffed
    MIN(patch_date)                                   AS first_change,
    MAX(patch_date)                                   AS last_change
FROM patch_changes
WHERE change_type <> 'new'
GROUP BY game, hero
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY total_changes DESC, hero) <= 5
ORDER BY game, total_changes DESC;
queries.takeaway: Most-patched: deadlock: Shiv (18 changes, 10 nerfs / 5 buffs); marvel-rivals: Gambit (11 changes, 7 nerfs / 1 buffs); overwatch: Vendetta (15 changes, 6 nerfs / 6 buffs).

queries.title: Rolling 30-day win-rate leaders by role (Deadlock)
queries.question: Right now, which heroes have the best match-weighted win rate over the last 30 days in each role?
queries.techniques: window aggregates with a RANGE frame (rolling sums), JOIN, QUALIFY + ROW_NUMBER per partition
queries.why: A rolling window smooths daily noise, and weighting by matches stops a low-volume day from swinging the number.
queries.sql:
WITH daily AS (
    SELECT d.date, d.hero, h.role, d.wins, d.matches
    FROM hero_daily d
    JOIN heroes h USING (game, hero)
    WHERE d.game = 'deadlock'
),
rolling AS (
    SELECT *,
        SUM(wins)    OVER w AS wins_30d,
        SUM(matches) OVER w AS matches_30d
    FROM daily
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY hero ORDER BY date
                 RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 29 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)
)
SELECT
    role,
    hero,
    ROUND(100.0 * wins_30d / matches_30d, 2) AS win_rate_30d,
    matches_30d
FROM rolling
WHERE date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM daily)
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY role ORDER BY wins_30d / matches_30d DESC) <= 3
ORDER BY role, win_rate_30d DESC;
queries.takeaway: Best 30-day win rate overall: Graves (Mystic) at 57.4% over 2,940,370 games.

queries.title: Patch whiplash: buffed, then nerfed within a month
queries.question: How often does a hero get changed one way and then reversed within 30 days?
queries.techniques: LAG() over an ordered partition, date arithmetic, filtering on window results
queries.why: Quick reversals point to over-corrections, a balance process that's reacting instead of predicting.
queries.sql:
WITH ordered AS (
    SELECT
        game, hero, patch_date, change_type,
        LAG(change_type) OVER w AS previous_change,
        LAG(patch_date)  OVER w AS previous_date
    FROM patch_changes
    WHERE change_type IN ('buff', 'nerf')
    WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY game, hero ORDER BY patch_date)
)
SELECT
    game,
    hero,
    previous_date,
    previous_change,
    patch_date                    AS reversed_on,
    change_type                   AS reversed_with,
    patch_date - previous_date    AS days_between
FROM ordered
WHERE previous_change IS NOT NULL
  AND previous_change <> change_type
  AND patch_date - previous_date <= 30
ORDER BY reversed_on DESC;
queries.takeaway: 91 reversals within 30 days (deadlock: 59, marvel-rivals: 21, overwatch: 11); 21 were reversed within a week.

queries.title: Do big patches bring players back?
queries.question: For each big patch (10+ heroes changed), how did average Steam players in the week after compare with the week before?
queries.techniques: CTEs, range join on dates, conditional aggregation, percentage change
queries.why: Ties balance work to a business outcome, player engagement, which is the question a game studio actually cares about.
queries.sql:
WITH big AS (
    SELECT game, patch_date, title, heroes_changed
    FROM patches
    WHERE heroes_changed >= 10
),
windows AS (
    SELECT
        b.game, b.patch_date, b.title, b.heroes_changed,
        AVG(p.avg_players) FILTER (WHERE p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date - 7 AND b.patch_date - 1) AS players_before,
        AVG(p.avg_players) FILTER (WHERE p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date + 1 AND b.patch_date + 7) AS players_after,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.date < b.patch_date) AS days_before,
        COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE p.date > b.patch_date) AS days_after
    FROM big b
    JOIN players_daily p
      ON p.game = b.game
     AND p.date BETWEEN b.patch_date - 7 AND b.patch_date + 7
    GROUP BY ALL
)
SELECT
    game,
    patch_date,
    title,
    heroes_changed,
    ROUND(players_before)                                          AS players_before,
    ROUND(players_after)                                           AS players_after,
    ROUND(100.0 * (players_after - players_before) / players_before, 1) AS pct_change
FROM windows
WHERE days_before >= 5 AND days_after >= 5      -- skip periods where only monthly history exists
ORDER BY patch_date DESC;
rows: Reign of Talon Season 5: A Grim Doctrine
queries.takeaway: Players rose in the week after 61% of big patches (median change +2.1%). Biggest jump: marvel-rivals, Season 11: Doomsday balance update (+35.9%).

queries.title: Which days are busiest?
queries.question: Relative to its own weekly average, how many more (or fewer) players does each game have on each day of the week?
queries.techniques: date functions (dayname, isodow, date_trunc), window AVG per week for normalization, complete-week filter
queries.why: Normalizing by week removes growth and decline trends, leaving the pure weekly rhythm. That's useful for timing events and patches.
queries.sql:
WITH d AS (
    SELECT
        game, date, avg_players,
        AVG(avg_players) OVER (PARTITION BY game, date_trunc('week', date)) AS week_mean,
        COUNT(*)         OVER (PARTITION BY game, date_trunc('week', date)) AS days_in_week
    FROM players_daily
    WHERE date >= (SELECT MAX(date) FROM players_daily) - INTERVAL 120 DAYS
)
SELECT
    game,
    dayname(date)                                        AS weekday,
    isodow(date)                                         AS day_number,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(avg_players / week_mean - 1), 1)   AS pct_vs_week_average,
    COUNT(*)                                             AS weeks_used
FROM d
WHERE days_in_week = 7                                   -- complete weeks only
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY game, day_number;
queries.takeaway: deadlock: busiest Sunday (+14%), quietest Monday (-7%); marvel-rivals: busiest Saturday (+11%), quietest Thursday (-10%); overwatch: busiest Sunday (+12%), quietest Thursday (-10%).

queries.title: Is the Deadlock meta getting more or less diverse?
queries.question: Each month, how concentrated are hero picks? Measured as the effective number of heroes (1 / HHI) and the top-5 share of all picks.
queries.techniques: window SUM for shares, ROW_NUMBER ranking, sum of squares (Herfindahl-Hirschman Index), monthly roll-up
queries.why: HHI is the economist's market-concentration measure. Here it turns "is the game balanced?" into a number you can track. Dividing by the roster size controls for new heroes being added.
queries.sql:
WITH shares AS (
    SELECT
        date, hero,
        matches * 1.0 / SUM(matches) OVER (PARTITION BY date) AS pick_share
    FROM hero_daily
    WHERE game = 'deadlock'
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY date ORDER BY pick_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM shares
),
per_day AS (
    SELECT
        date,
        SUM(pick_share * pick_share)              AS hhi,
        SUM(pick_share) FILTER (WHERE rk <= 5)    AS top5_share,
        COUNT(*)                                  AS heroes_played
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY date
)
SELECT
    strftime(date_trunc('month', date), '%Y-%m') AS month,
    ROUND(AVG(1 / hhi), 1)                       AS effective_heroes,
    MAX(heroes_played)                           AS heroes_available,
    ROUND(100 * AVG((1 / hhi) / heroes_played), 1) AS diversity_pct_of_roster,   -- 100% = every hero picked equally
    ROUND(100 * AVG(top5_share), 1)              AS top5_pick_share_pct
FROM per_day
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;
queries.takeaway: Effective heroes went from 28.2 (2025-10) to 38.8 (2026-11), but relative to roster size diversity moved only from 88.1% to 88.3%: the rise comes from new heroes being added, not from a more balanced meta.

queries.title: Do players ban the right heroes?
queries.question: In Overwatch and Marvel Rivals, how strongly does ban rate track win rate and pick rate? Which heroes are banned the most despite a below-average win rate?
queries.techniques: CORR(), arg_max, PERCENT_RANK window, latest-snapshot filter
queries.why: Bans are a player perception signal. Comparing them with results shows where perception and data disagree.
queries.sql:
WITH latest AS (
    SELECT *
    FROM hero_daily
    WHERE game IN ('overwatch', 'marvel-rivals')
      AND ban_rate IS NOT NULL
    QUALIFY date = MAX(date) OVER (PARTITION BY game)
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
        PERCENT_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY game ORDER BY ban_rate) AS ban_pctile,
        AVG(win_rate)  OVER (PARTITION BY game)                   AS game_avg_wr
    FROM latest
)
SELECT
    game,
    COUNT(*)                                         AS heroes,
    ROUND(CORR(ban_rate, win_rate), 2)               AS corr_ban_vs_win,
    ROUND(CORR(ban_rate, pick_rate), 2)              AS corr_ban_vs_pick,
    arg_max(hero, ban_rate)                          AS most_banned,
    ROUND(MAX(ban_rate), 1)                          AS top_ban_rate,
    string_agg(hero, ', ' ORDER BY ban_rate DESC)
        FILTER (WHERE ban_pctile >= 0.8 AND win_rate < game_avg_wr) AS overbanned_below_avg_wr
FROM ranked
GROUP BY game
ORDER BY game;
rows: Phoenix, Spider-Man, Elsa Bloodstone, Gambit, Emma Frost, Winter Soldier, Namor
Zarya, Jetpack Cat, Roadhog, Orisa, Mauga, Ana
queries.takeaway: marvel-rivals: ban vs. win-rate correlation +0.06, most banned Devil Dinosaur (36%). overwatch: ban vs. win-rate correlation -0.02, most banned Zarya (39%). Bans track perception more than results.

queries.title: Underused team-up loadouts (Marvel Rivals)
queries.question: For which heroes does the less popular team-up loadout have a higher win rate with its partner than the popular one?
queries.techniques: ROW_NUMBER, pivot with conditional MAX(CASE ...), derived comparison column
queries.why: A gap between popularity and performance is an "insight you can act on": a free win-rate edge most players are ignoring.
queries.sql:
WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT *, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY hero ORDER BY usage_share DESC) AS rk
    FROM teamups
    WHERE usage_share IS NOT NULL
),
pivoted AS (
    SELECT
        hero,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN loadout END)          AS popular_loadout,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN usage_share END)      AS popular_share,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 1 THEN wr_with_partner END)  AS popular_wr_with_partner,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN loadout END)          AS other_loadout,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN usage_share END)      AS other_share,
        MAX(CASE WHEN rk = 2 THEN wr_with_partner END)  AS other_wr_with_partner
    FROM ranked
    GROUP BY hero
)
SELECT
    hero,
    popular_loadout,
    ROUND(popular_share, 1)                                        AS popular_share_pct,
    ROUND(popular_wr_with_partner, 1)                              AS popular_wr,
    other_loadout,
    ROUND(other_share, 1)                                          AS other_share_pct,
    ROUND(other_wr_with_partner, 1)                                AS other_wr,
    ROUND(other_wr_with_partner - popular_wr_with_partner, 1)      AS other_loadout_edge
FROM pivoted
WHERE other_wr_with_partner > popular_wr_with_partner
  AND hero NOT LIKE 'Deadpool (%'          -- Deadpool's three role variants share one set of loadouts
ORDER BY other_loadout_edge DESC
LIMIT 12;
queries.takeaway: 12 heroes have an underused loadout that wins more often. Biggest gap: Groot's Wild Wall (36% usage) wins +10.3 pts more than Bubble Buddies.

queries.title: Data quality check: do the matchup numbers agree with each other?
queries.question: If hero A wins X% against hero B, then B should win (100 - X)% against A, over the same number of games. Does the matchup data pass that test?
queries.techniques: self-join, symmetric pair de-duplication (a.hero < a.enemy), validation metrics
queries.why: Checking a source against its own logic before trusting it is basic data-quality practice, and an easy way to catch a broken feed.
queries.sql:
SELECT
    COUNT(*)                                                       AS hero_pairs_checked,
    ROUND(AVG(ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100)), 3)              AS avg_deviation_pts,
    ROUND(MAX(ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100)), 3)              AS max_deviation_pts,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE a.matches = b.matches)                  AS pairs_with_equal_game_counts,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE ABS(a.win_rate + b.win_rate - 100) > 0.5) AS pairs_failing_0_5pt_tolerance
FROM matchups a
JOIN matchups b
  ON a.game = b.game
 AND a.hero = b.enemy
 AND a.enemy = b.hero
WHERE a.hero < a.enemy;
queries.takeaway: PASS: 946 matchup pairs; average deviation 0.014 pts, max 0.04 pts, 0 outside a 0.5-pt tolerance.

queries.title: This week's biggest movers (Deadlock) and whether a patch explains them
queries.question: Which heroes' win rates changed most between the last 7 days and the 7 days before? Was each mover patched in that period?
queries.techniques: date-bounded CTEs, conditional aggregation, LEFT JOIN with string_agg, UNION ALL of top/bottom ranks
queries.why: Separating "moved because of a patch" from "moved on its own" is the first question to ask about any metric change.
queries.sql:
WITH bounds AS (
    SELECT MAX(date) AS last_day FROM hero_daily WHERE game = 'deadlock'
),
weekly AS (
    SELECT
        d.hero,
        SUM(d.wins)    FILTER (WHERE d.date >  b.last_day - 7)                              AS wins_now,
        SUM(d.matches) FILTER (WHERE d.date >  b.last_day - 7)                              AS games_now,
        SUM(d.wins)    FILTER (WHERE d.date <= b.last_day - 7 AND d.date > b.last_day - 14) AS wins_prev,
        SUM(d.matches) FILTER (WHERE d.date <= b.last_day - 7 AND d.date > b.last_day - 14) AS games_prev
    FROM hero_daily d, bounds b
    WHERE d.game = 'deadlock'
    GROUP BY d.hero
),
moves AS (
    SELECT
        hero,
        100.0 * wins_now / games_now   AS wr_now,
        100.0 * wins_prev / games_prev AS wr_prev,
        100.0 * wins_now / games_now - 100.0 * wins_prev / games_prev AS change_pts,
        games_now
    FROM weekly
    WHERE games_now >= 5000 AND games_prev >= 5000
),
ranked AS (
    SELECT *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY change_pts DESC) AS up_rank,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY change_pts ASC)  AS down_rank
    FROM moves
),
patched AS (
    SELECT c.hero, string_agg(c.change_type || ' (' || strftime(c.patch_date, '%b %d') || ')', ', ') AS recent_patch
    FROM patch_changes c, bounds b
    WHERE c.game = 'deadlock' AND c.patch_date > b.last_day - 14
    GROUP BY c.hero
)
SELECT
    CASE WHEN up_rank <= 5 THEN 'riser' ELSE 'faller' END AS direction,
    r.hero,
    ROUND(wr_prev, 2)    AS win_rate_prev_week,
    ROUND(wr_now, 2)     AS win_rate_this_week,
    ROUND(change_pts, 2) AS change_pts,
    games_now            AS games_this_week,
    COALESCE(p.recent_patch, 'no patch: moved on its own') AS explained_by
FROM ranked r
LEFT JOIN patched p USING (hero)
WHERE up_rank <= 5 OR down_rank <= 5
ORDER BY change_pts DESC;
